sections.h2: Where is Agawam and what is it like?
sections.html:
Agawam sits in Hampden County on the west bank of the Connecticut River, directly across from Springfield, and about 28,700 people lived there at the 2020 census.

The city covers 24.34 square miles. It touches West Springfield to the north, Southwick and Westfield to the west, Longmeadow and Springfield to the east, and Suffield, Connecticut to the south. Provin Mountain, at 640 feet, is the high point and anchors a trap rock ridge that forms the western edge of town. Feeding Hills, the western section along the Southwick and Westfield lines, carries its own ZIP code, 01030. The main Agawam ZIP, 01001, is the lowest standard ZIP code in the continental United States.

Agawam is a mayor-council city that still uses "Town of Agawam" in its official name.

It adopted a city charter effective January 1, 1973, and has elected a mayor since May 1989. Eleven council members, all elected at large, make up the legislative branch. For a seller, the council matters on one point in particular: according to the town's own FAQ, the decision to split the tax burden among property classes is made each year by the Town Council with the Mayor's approval.

sections.h2: How does Agawam's history show up in the housing stock?
sections.html:
Agawam was a small mill and distillery town for much of its history, then added residents quickly after the Second World War.

Population was under 8,000 in 1940 and passed 15,000 by 1960 and 21,000 by 1970. It has hovered between roughly 28,000 and 28,700 since 2000. Most of that growth came in the decades after 1940, so many homes date from the postwar boom, with older buildings in the village centers.

Some of the land has changed use. The Bowles Agawam Airport and the racetrack beside it were demolished in the late 1980s, and the area is an industrial park now. Six Flags New England stands on the river site where a cotton mill was built in 1810.

sections.h2: Which schools and parks serve Agawam homes?
sections.html:
Agawam runs its own school district, and buyers often start there when they compare towns.

  • Four elementary schools for kindergarten through grade 4: Benjamin J. Phelps, Clifford M. Granger, James Clark and William P. Sapelli
  • Roberta G. Doering Middle School for grades 5 and 6
  • Agawam Junior High for grades 7 and 8
  • Agawam High School for grades 9 through 12

For outdoor space, the city has Robinson State Park, a narrow 852-acre park entered from North Street, and a stretch of the 110-mile Metacomet-Monadnock Trail along Provin Mountain. The Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery is off Main Street.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Agawam?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office at 36 Main Street handles values, abatements and mailing address changes, and you can reach it at 413-786-0400, extension 8700.

The town's real estate tax FAQ says the assessor values every parcel as of each January 1, using market, income and cost approaches. Ownership changes follow the recorded deed: the office receives deeds recorded at the Hampden County Registry of Deeds, and a new owner's name usually appears on the next billing cycle. If it does not, call the office.

We did not find a current tax rate or bill due dates on an official Agawam page we could open, so we leave those out. Ask the Assessor or the Collector for the exact schedule and payoff amount before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How do you contest an Agawam assessment?
sections.html:
You file an application for abatement, and for fiscal year 2026 the town set the deadline at 4:30 pm on February 1, 2026.

The application becomes available right after the first actual bill, which is the third quarter bill. A mailed application must carry a postmark dated no later than the deadline, and the assessors say they cannot waive it. The grounds listed by the town are overvaluation, disproportionate assessment, misclassification and a statutory exemption.

  • Pay each installment on time while the request is pending.
  • Gather recent sales of similar homes nearby and note the condition of each.
  • If the assessors deny the request or do not act, the state's Appellate Tax Board guide sets a three-month window to appeal.

sections.h2: What can go wrong if you fall behind on Agawam taxes?
sections.html:
An unpaid tax bill turns into a lien, and the city can eventually record a tax taking.

The Land Court's tax lien foreclosure overview explains the sequence. After a bill sits unpaid for 30 days, a demand can go out. If it stays unpaid 14 days after that, a taking can be recorded at the Registry of Deeds. An owner can still redeem by paying everything owed until the court enters a judgment of foreclosure. For an owner who cannot catch up, a sale before the taking or before judgment keeps equity in play.

sections.h2: What paperwork does an Agawam sale need?
sections.html:
Two items come up on nearly every Agawam closing: a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate, and clean ownership records.

  • The Department of Fire Services says a one or two family home needs a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing the alarms meet requirements for a sale. Its guide tells owners to schedule the inspection once there is a closing date, and the department charges a fee.
  • Battery-powered smoke alarms over 10 years old, or expired, must be replaced with sealed 10-year photoelectric models that have a hush feature.
  • The deed is recorded at the Hampden County Registry of Deeds, and the assessor's records follow it.

Deed excise tax is set by state law and collected by the registry. Ask the registry or your closing attorney for the current figure on your sale price.

sections.h2: What do Agawam sellers usually weigh?
sections.html:
Most owners compare a traditional listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a direct cash offer.

A listing can reach the widest pool of buyers, but it can bring repair requests, showings and a wait for a buyer's financing. A direct cash purchase usually trims that timeline and lets the owner sell the house in its current condition, which suits inherited homes, rentals with problem tenants and houses that need roof or system work. The price is usually lower than a fully prepared listing would bring, so compare the net, not just the headline number.

Whichever route you choose, confirm what you owe in taxes, ask for the offer in writing, and give yourself time to read the contract.

faqs.q: Is Agawam a town or a city?
faqs.a: Both. Agawam has had a city form of government since January 1, 1973, with a mayor and council, but it keeps "Town of Agawam" as its official name.

faqs.q: Where do I file an Agawam property tax abatement?
faqs.a: With the Assessor's Office at 36 Main Street. For fiscal year 2026 the application was due by 4:30 pm on February 1, 2026, and mailed forms needed a postmark by that date.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a change of owner on my Agawam tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at 413-786-0400, extension 8700. The office updates ownership from deeds recorded at the Hampden County Registry of Deeds, usually by the next billing cycle.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector certificate to sell my Agawam house?
faqs.a: For a one or two family home, yes. The local fire department issues a certificate of compliance for sale, and you should schedule it when you have a closing date.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Agawam house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A direct buyer can purchase a house as it stands, though the price reflects the work needed. A listing may bring a higher price but often expects repairs first.

faqs.q: What happens to an Agawam tax lien when I sell?
faqs.a: The amount owed is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the city for a written payoff before the closing date.
